This suit is filed by the plaintiff against defendant Nos.1 to 5 for permanent injunction restraining the defendant from interfering in O.S.No.3617/2020 his peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.

The suit schedule property is vacant site bearing Nos.13 and 14, katha Nos.264/1/13-14 assessment No.50/1, formerly house list katha No.264/1, situated at K.Narayanapura Village, K.R.Puram Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk, now coming under the limits of BBMP measuring East to West 58 ft on the Southern side 42 ft on Northern side, North to South 40ft, totally measuring 2000 sq.ft, bounded on East by site No.50, West road, North road, South site Nos.11 and 12.
This property herein after referred as suit property for brevity.

2. The case of the plaintiff unfolds as follows:-
The plaintiff claimed that he is the absolute owner and possessor of suit property having acquired the same through registered Gift Deed, dated 16-10-2017 executed by his mother Smt.Najma Nazneen.
After getting the suit property, katha was transferred in his name in the BBMP records and he is paying the property tax up to date.

sentences.text: According to the plaintiff, this property was purchased by her mother from Mohammed Inayath and Mohammed Siraj by virtue of sale deed dated 7-11-2014.
After purchasing the property, the katha O.S.No.3617/2020 was changed in the name of his mother Nazma Nazneen and she was paying the property tax.
The plaintiff contended that on 11-3-2020, with a view of putting up construction, he engaged workers for cleaning the suit schedule property.
On 12-03-2020, the mother of the plaintiff was receiving threatening calls from a specific mobile number mentioned in para No.4 of the plaint.
Therefore, she filed complaint on 16-3- 2020 requesting the police to solve the problem.
The Kothanur police had issued NCR No.111/2020.
Because of Covid-19 he could not pursue the matter.
On 3-7-2020, the plaintiff hired the laborers for cleaning the grass and garbage in the suit property.
The defendants trespassed in the suit property threatened the plaintiff not to commence the work of cleaning the suit property.
They abused the plaintiff in vulgar language and threatened dire consequences.
The plaintiff and his mother have submitted complaint to Kothanur police station through email on 4-7-2020.
The physical complaint was also filed before the Commissioner of Police on the same day.
But the police have not taken any action against the defendants.
Therefore, the plaintiff has filed suit for permanent injunction against the defendants sought to decree the suit.
The suit summons issued to the defendants.
Defendant No.3 was placed exparte, the other defendants appeared through their counsel.
The defendant No.2 and 5 have filed the written statement.
The defendant Nos.2 and 5 have specifically denied the case of the plaintiff.
It is the case of defendant Nos.2 and 5 that one Munishamappa @ Bedarahalli Munishamppa was an agriculturist, he acquired several agricultural properties.
He had five children.

Those are Nagamma,
Muniyappa,Pillamma, Eramma and Appanna Gowda.
The defendant No.3 is the son of Appanna Gowda.
The defendant Nos.2 and 5 contended that Munishamappa @ Bedharahalli Munishamappa during his life time acquired Sy.No.50/1 measuring 1 acre 11 guntas of K.Narayanapura Village.
The said Survey Number was allotted to Munishamappa @ Bidharahalli Munishamappa on behalf of the joint family by Spl.Dy.Commissioner of Abolition of Inams in case No.35/1956-57.
These defendants contended that Munishamappa died intestate leaving behind his wife and five children as joint family members.
The other children of Munishamappa are innocent.
The father of defendant No.3 Appanna Gowda was only having worldly knowledge and managing the family affairs after the death of the propositus of Munishamappa.
The defendant Nos.2 and 5 contended that they are in joint possession and enjoyment of Sy.No.50/1 along with other defendants.

They contended that the katha of the suit Nabeel Sarosh vs Santhosh S on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32726703/

they contended that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:-
The burden of proving the issues Nos.1 to 3 is on the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has filed suit for injunction simplicitor claiming that the suit property was gifted to him by his mother Nazma Nazneen by virtue of the registered Gift Deed, dated 16-10-2017.
In order to prove that on the date of filing of the suit, he is in possession and enjoyment of suit property.
He produced Rent Agreements, electricity bills, tax paid receipts, photographs, the sale deed and registered Gift Deed.

Ex.P.13 and Ex.D.6 are the same documents i.e., the Gift Deed, dated 16-10- 2017 executed by the mother of the plaintiff in favour of the plaintiff by gifting the suit property totally measuring 2000 sq.ft carved out in Sy.No.50/1 of K.Narayanapura Village.
The majority of the documents are produced by the defendants and marked as Exs.D.3 to D.6 which clarifies the title and possession of the plaintiff over the suit property.

The flow of title to the suit property starts from M.Appanna Gowda who claims to be the uncle of defendant Nos.2 and 5.
Appanna Gowda claims that he is the owner and possessor of the 17 guntas of property in Sy.No.50/1 and he sold a portion of property measuring 2610 sq.ft of property in case of Thankam Nambiyar through registered sale deed dated 16-5-2000.
It is the responsibility of the plaintiff to produce all the documents.
However, the work of plaintiff was reduced by the defendants by producing Ex.D.2.
Ex.D.2 is the sale deed executed by M.Appanna Gowda in favour of Thankam Nambiar.
10. In page No.2, the uncle of the defendant No.1 stated that he derived the property from his ancestors and he is selling an area of 2610 sq.ft in Sy.No.50/1.
The site number, house list katha number and the measurement mentioned in the sale deed are identical with the suit property.
However, the extent mentioned in the Ex.D.2 is 2610 sq.ft, whereas, in other sale deeds, the extent is reduced only to the 2000 sq.ft.
After execution of the sale deeds, in the year 2000, Thankam Nambiar becomes owner and possessor of O.S.No.3617/2020 the site Nos.13 and 14, house list No.264/1.
After 8 years, Thankam Nambiar has sold the reduced extent of 2000 sq.ft by virtue of Ex.D.3 i.e., registered sale deed, dated 1-1-2008 in favour of Mohammed Inayath, Mohammed Rizwan, Mohammed Siraj.
The contents of the documents again reveals that this property derived from Appanna Gowda.
There is clear recitals in it.
Subsequently, one of the joint purchaser Mohammed Rizwan has sold his 1/3 rd share to Mohammed Siraj by virtue of sale deed, dated 14-02-2013.
This sale deed is also produced by the defendants and marked as Ex.D.4.

Therefore,
Mohammed Inayath and Mohammed Siraj became owner to the extent of 1/3rd and 2/3rd shares.
Both of them have jointly executed sale deed on 7-11-2014 as per Ex.D.5 in favour of Nazma Nazneen i.e., the mother of the plaintiff.
Smt.Nazma Nazneen, the mother of the plaintiff has executed Gift Deed on 16-10-2017 in favour of the plaintiff as per Ex.P.13 and Ex.D.6.

In all these sale deeds and Gift Deeds, the property number and the boundaries mentioned to the property is Nabeel Sarosh vs Santhosh S on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32726703/
5 identical and there is a clear flow of title from M.Appanna Gowda to the plaintiff.

sentences.text: 11. The plaintiff has produced the tax paid receipts, rent agreement, photographs to show that he is in possession and O.S.No.3617/2020 enjoyment of the suit property.
The defendants claimed that they are in possession and enjoyment of the suit property.
12. The learned counsel for the defendant highlighted the cross-examination of P.W.1.
In the cross-examination of P.W.1, in page No.10, first para, the P.W.1 admitted that the suit property is situated in Sy.No.5/1.
It may be an omission because in the subsequent cross-examination, he stated that the property comes under Sy.No.50/1.
According to the cross-examination of P.W.1 he states that the defendants caused interference in his possession in the month of July 2020.

13. The learned counsel for the defendants also highlighted para No.4, page No.12 of the cross-examination of P.W.1, wherein he stated that he is not aware in which direction, the Sy.No.50/1 the suit schedule property is situated.
He denied the suggestion that entire property in Sy.No.50/1 is still a vacant site which is under the control of BDA.
14. The learned counsel for the defendants also highlighted the para No.5 of cross-examination of P.W.1, wherein, he was unable to spell the boundaries of the suit property.
Based on these O.S.No.3617/2020 cross-examinations, learned counsel for the defendant argued that the cross-examination of P.W.1 goes to show that he is not at all in possession of suit property.

But, on the contrary, the property tax received by the BBMP and the other documents produced by the plaintiff reveals that the is in possession and enjoyment of suit property as on the date of filing of the suit.
15. Apart from it, the Ex.P.14 was confronted to D.W.1 during the cross-examination, wherein, he admitted the signatures of his family members and admitted the contents of the document.
Ex.P.14 is the photo copy of the Memorandum of Partition entered between the family members of Munishamappa wherein, in page No.4, the properties acquired by Appanna Gowda is mentioned.
The item No.2 is land Sy.No.50/1 measuring 17 guntas allotted to Appanna Gowda with specific boundaries mentioned in it.

This clearly goes to show that M.Appanna Gowda has 17 guntas of property in Sy.No.50/1 which is subsequently sold to Thankam Nambiar as per Ex.D.2.
16.
The defendants relied upon Ex.D.1 which is the RTC.
It shows that 1 acre 3 guntas standing in the name of Muniyamma, Muniyappa and Appanna Gowda jointly.
8 guntas of property O.S.No.3617/2020 standing in the name of Sridevi Wife A.Chinnanna.
In column No.11 of Ex.D.1 it is mentioned that out of 1 acre 18 guntas of land, 7 guntas is karab and 1 acre of land was acquired by BDA.
According to learned counsel for the defendants, 1 acre was acquired by BDA, 8 guntas belonging to Sridevi and 7 guntas is karab.
Therefore, the property claimed by the plaintiff is fictitious property and M.Appanna Gowda has no right to execute the sale deed in favour of Thankam Nambiar.
But, the sale deed executed by Appanna Gowda in favour of Thankam Nambiar is on 16-5-2000 but the date of acquisition mentioned in the Ex.D.1 is 21-2-2004.
By the time, this sale deed was executed, the vendor of the Thankam Nambiar alienated 2610 sq.ft in his 17 guntas of property.
It is for the BDA to take action against the occupants of the 1 acre of acquired land.

Even in Nabeel Sarosh vs Santhosh S on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32726703/
6 the worst situation, the defendants are not at all the owners and possessors because 1 acre was acquired by the BDA, 8 guntas standing in the name of Sridevi and 7 guntas is karab.

sentences.text: The defendants cannot claim ownership over 7 guntas or ownership over the 8 guntas of property standing in the name of Sridevi.
It seems that she is not the family member of the defendants.

During the cross-examination of D.W.1, he stated that 1 acre of land was acquired by the BDA and his father and uncles have not filed any O.S.No.3617/2020 application to drop the acquisition proceedings.
The compensation amount is deposited before the BDA.
Since the case is pending they have not taken the compensation amount.

If the defendants are entitled they can claim the compensation amount but they are not the owners or possessors of the entire Sy.No.50/1.
17.

In cross-examination of D.W.1 at page No.10, para No.7, he denied the execution of sale deed from Appanna Gowda to Thankam Nambiar, Thankam Nambiar to Mohammed Inayath,
Mohammed Rizwan and Mohammed Siraj.

Subsequently, sale deed executed by Mohammed Rizwan in favour of Mohammed Siraj and Mohammed Inayath, Mohammed Siraj in favour of the mother of plaintiff but contrary to his evidence, he himself has produced Exs.D.2 to D.6 by reducing the burden of plaintiff to prove the possession.
These Exs.D.2 to D.6 clarifies that there is a clear flow of title from M.Appanna Gowda to the plaintiff through registered instruments.
It may be a fact that the extent of land is reduced to 2000 sq.ft from Ex.D.3 to D.6.
But on perusal of the oral and documentary evidence, it is clear that as on the date of filing of the suit, the plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of the suit property.
The complaint filed by the mother of the plaintiff and the plaintiff goes O.S.No.3617/2020 to show that there is a actual interference by the defendants in the possession of the plaintiff.

There is no need to file a comprehensive suit for declaration or possession by the plaintiff because the documents reveal that there is a clear flow of title in favour of the plaintiff by registered instruments.
Therefore, the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anathula Sudhakar vs P. Buchi Reddy (Dead) By Lrs & Ors reported in AIR 2008 SC 2033 cannot be pressed into service in this case.

18. Issue No.4:-

For the foregoing reasons, I pass the following:-
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff decreed with costs.
The defendants restrained by way of permanent injunction from interfering in the possession and enjoyment of the plaintiff over the suit property.
Draw decree accordingly.
